title: FastCF
text:
fastcflare provides an async Cloudflare API client built from Cloudflare’s OpenAPI schema. Use CloudflareApi to browse API operations, manage zones and DNS records, and create scoped tokens. The examples below show user-token access and account-owned tokens.
from fastcore.utils import *
from fastcflare import *

title: FastCF
text:
Quickstart

from fastcflare import *


usrtok = os.environ['CLOUDFLARE_USR_TOK']


ucf = CloudflareApi(token=usrtok)
(await ucf.verify()).result.status

'active'



(await ucf.zones.list()).result[0].name

'aaa.as'



Create a token
Create a token with Zone Read and DNS Write permissions for one domain. Replace xxx with the domain name. The client used to create it must have permission to create tokens:
doms = ['xxx']
pnms = ('Zone Read', 'DNS Write')
tok = await ucf.create_token(doms, pnms, 'domain mgt')
dns_token = tok.result.value
Store the token securely. For APIs that accept a Global API Key, construct the client with CloudflareApi(email=os.environ['CLOUDFLARE_EML_ADD'], api_key=os.environ['CLOUDFLARE_API_KEY']) instead.
Use the new token to list DNS records, create a test A record, and delete that record. This changes DNS records in an existing zone; it does not create or delete the domain:
domnm = 'xxx'
zones = (await ucf.zones.list(name=domnm)).result
zid_sp = zones[0].id

dcf = CloudflareApi(token=dns_token)
print((await dcf.zones.dns_records.list(zone_id=zid_sp)).result[:3])
rec = await dcf.zones.dns_records.post(zid_sp, type='A', name='test-delete-me.xxx', content='192.0.2.1', ttl=1)
print(rec.result.id, rec.result.name)
print((await dcf.zones.dns_records.delete(zid_sp, rec.result.id)).result.id)

title: FastCF
text:
Intro to Account Tokens
Account-owned API tokens belong to an account and act as service principals with their own permissions. They support CI/CD and service integrations that need to keep working after the creating user leaves the organization. The API endpoint is /accounts/{id}/tokens.

Creating Account Tokens
Cloudflare requires Super Administrator permission to create or update account-owned tokens. The creation endpoint accepts an API token with Account API Tokens Write. The following example uses the official Cloudflare Python SDK with token authentication:
from cloudflare import Cloudflare
cf = Cloudflare(api_token=your_cf_token)
accts = cf.accounts.list()
acct_id = next(iter(accts)).id
Look up permission groups available to the account:
groups = list(cf.accounts.tokens.permission_groups.list(account_id=acct_id))
{g.name: g.id for g in groups if 'dns' in g.name.lower() or 'zone' in g.name.lower()}
For account-owned tokens, nest zone resources under the account resource. This example grants Zone Read and DNS Write across its zones:
tok = cf.accounts.tokens.create(account_id=acct_id, name="dns-all-zones", policies=[{
    "effect": "allow",
    "resources": {f"com.cloudflare.api.account.{acct_id}": {"com.cloudflare.api.account.zone.*": "*"}},
    "permission_groups": [{"id": g.id} for g in groups if g.name in ('Zone Read', 'DNS Write')]
}])
dns_tok = tok.value  # Store securely; the value is only returned at creation
A zone resource without the enclosing account, such as {"com.cloudflare.api.account.zone.*": "*"}, fails with: “Must specify a zone for account owned tokens, or nest zone under specific account resource”. Keep the nested format even when granting access to all zones.

title: FastCF
text:
Development
The op surface comes from cf_spec.py, Cloudflare’s OpenAPI schema in fastspec’s compact form. Refresh it from Cloudflare’s published schema with tools/build.py, then review the diff: op names can shift when the schema changes.

title: fastcflare
text:
import httpx
from collections import Counter


acctok = os.getenv('CLOUDFLARE_ACC_TOK')
usrtok = os.environ['CLOUDFLARE_USR_TOK']
acctid = os.getenv('CLOUDFLARE_ACCT_ID')
acceml = os.getenv('CLOUDFLARE_EML_ADD')


base = 'https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4'


uhdrs = {'Authorization': f'Bearer {usrtok}'}
r = httpx.get(f'{base}/user/tokens/verify', headers=uhdrs)
r.json()['success']

True



if acctok and acctid:
    ahdrs = {'Authorization': f'Bearer {acctok}'}
    r = httpx.get(f'{base}/accounts/{acctid}/tokens/verify', headers=ahdrs)
    print(r.json()['success'])

True



glbtok = os.getenv('CLOUDFLARE_API_KEY')
if acceml and glbtok:
    ghdrs = {'X-Auth-Email': acceml, 'X-Auth-Key': glbtok, 'Content-Type': 'application/json'}
    r = httpx.get(f'{base}/user', headers=ghdrs)
    print(r.json()['success'])

True



r = httpx.get(f'{base}/zones', headers=uhdrs)
[(z['name'], z['id'][:8]) for z in r.json()['result'][:1]]

[('aaa.as', '6afde8dc')]



if acctok and acctid:
    r = httpx.get(f'{base}/zones', headers=ahdrs, params={'account.id': acctid})
    print([(z['name'], z['id'][:8]) for z in r.json()['result'][:1]])

[('aaa.as', '6afde8dc')]

title: fastcflare
text:
CloudflareApi
Cloudflare’s operationIds are machine artifacts (zones-get vs zones-0-get — the -0- is a generator’s dedup counter), so rather than cleaning them up we name every op mechanically from its verb and path: the group is the path’s non-parameter segments, nested (zones.dns_records), and the method is the HTTP verb — except that when a group has both a collection GET and a single-item GET they become list and get. Two fixups keep the whole surface collision-free: sibling paths differing only by an interior parameter gain a _by_<param> suffix, and an action segment that would shadow an op folds into its parent as <segment>_<verb>. So GET /zones is zones.list, GET /zones/{zone_id} is zones.get, and GET /user/tokens/verify is user.tokens.verify.get — a user who knows the URL knows the call.


source

    spec

Map each op’s canonical (verb, snaked-segments) key to (group_segments, op_name), collision-free across the surface




source

cf_group_func

    names
):
A fastspec group_func looking up precomputed names by canonical verb+path


The parsed surface ships with the package as cf_spec.py, fastspec’s compact form (SpecParser.save): 2.6MB instead of the 8MB raw schema, loaded in ~30ms instead of a ~0.3s parse, with the naming machinery above running only at regeneration time. build_spec refreshes it from Cloudflare’s published schema; op names can shift when the spec changes, so review that diff before shipping it.


source

build_spec
def build_spec(
    nm:str='fastcflare/cf_spec.py',
    url:str='https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cloudflare/api-schemas/main/openapi.json'
):
Regenerate the compact spec module cf_spec.py from Cloudflare’s OpenAPI schema.



cli = OpenAPIClient(_cf_spec(), headers={'Authorization': f'Bearer {usrtok}', 'Content-Type': 'application/json'})
sorted(cli.groups)

['accounts',
 'certificates',
 'internal',
 'ips',
 'live',
 'memberships',
 'organizations',
 'radar',
 'ready',
 'signed_url',
 'system',
 'tenants',
 'user',
 'users',
 'zones']


The naming is only trustworthy if it can never silently collide — OpGroup exposes ops with setattr, so a duplicate name would shadow its sibling (exactly the bug this design replaces). This walk asserts the built tree is clean: within every group, op names are unique (duplicates allowed only for the same endpoint spelled two ways in the spec) and no op shares a name with a subgroup.

def _surface_ok(g):
    nms = [o.name for o in g.ops]
    for n,c in Counter(nms).items():
        if c>1: assert len({tuple(snake(s) for s in o.op_spec.path.strip('/').split('/')) for o in g.ops if o.name==n})==1, f'dup op {g.name}.{n}'
    assert not set(nms)&set(g.subgroups), f'op/subgroup shadow in {g.name}: {set(nms)&set(g.subgroups)}'
    for sg in g.subgroups.values(): _surface_ok(sg)

for grp in cli.groups.values(): _surface_ok(grp)
len(cli.groups), len(cli.groups['zones'].subgroups)

(15, 60)

CloudflareApi
def CloudflareApi(
    token:NoneType=None, # API token, defaulting to `CF_API_TOKEN` when neither `token` nor `api_key` is given
    account_id:NoneType=None, # Account that owns the token, for account-owned tokens
    email:NoneType=None, # Account email for a global API key, defaulting to `CF_API_EMAIL`
    api_key:NoneType=None, # Global API key, used with `email` in place of a token
):
Cloudflare API client supporting both user and account tokens



ucf = CloudflareApi(token=usrtok)
(await ucf.verify()).result.status

'active'



if acctok and acctid:
    acf = CloudflareApi(token=acctok, account_id=acctid)
    print((await acf.verify()).result.status)

active


Listing and fetching zones are now distinct calls: zones.list filters the collection, zones.get takes a zone_id.

ucf.zones.list

List Zones
Parameters: - name (str, optional) - status (str, optional) - account_id (str, optional) - account_name (str, optional) - order (str, optional) - direction (str, optional) - page (float, default: 1) - per_page (float, default: 20) - match (str, default: ‘all’)



(await ucf.zones.list(name='answer.ai')).result[0].name

'answer.ai'

CloudflareApi.create_token
async def create_token(
    doms, # Domain names the token may act on
    perm_names, # Permission-group names, such as 'Zone Read' or 'DNS Write'. Names that don't match are skipped
    name, # Name for the new token
    grp:str='account.zone.', # Resource prefix after `com.cloudflare.api.`
):
Create a user API token limited to doms. The token’s value is shown only in this response.



pgs = (await ucf.user.tokens.permission_groups.get()).result
[p.name for p in pgs if 'DNS' in p.name or 'Zone' in p.name][:20]

['Account DNS Settings Read',
 'Account DNS Settings Write',
 'Cloudflare Zero Trust Secure DNS Locations Write',
 'DNS Firewall Read',
 'DNS Firewall Write',
 'DNS Read',
 'DNS View Read',
 'DNS View Write',

With two domains, the policy must carry two distinct zone resources — under the old colliding surface the name filter was silently dropped, every domain resolved to the same zone, and the dict collapsed them to one:

tok = await ucf.create_token(['answer.ai', 'aaa.as'], ['Zone Read'], 'fastcflare-test-token')
assert len(tok.result.policies[0].resources)==2
tok.success, tok.result.name

(True, 'fastcflare-test-token')


Clean up the token we just created:

res = await ucf.user.tokens.delete(tok.result.id)
assert res.success
